tx_reimers_ranch.blurb: Reimers Ranch is a county park on the Pedernales River, roughly 30 miles from Austin, and the city's best-known sport climbing venue. The rock is pocketed limestone, and the climbing is overwhelmingly sport, with a small amount of bouldering and a few top ropes. Routes span slabs to roofs; the grades center on 5.10 to 5.12 with a good number of 5.9s and a hard tail up to 5.14. Grades can feel stiff, and the pale rock hides chalk, which makes onsighting harder. Holds stay wet for days after rain. Climbing is possible year round. Dead Cats Wall draws weekend crowds, while Arbor Wall and Hand Beyond Wall are alternatives.

ca_wonderland_south.blurb: Wonderland South is the southern end of the Wonderland of Rocks in Joshua Tree National Park, north and east of the Barker Dam area. The terrain is a maze of domes, towers, arches and grottos with a huge amount of rock and complicated topography. Trad climbing dominates, with some sport and top-rope routes and very little bouldering. Grades center on 5.9 to 5.11, with a spread of easier lines and a few at 5.12 and 5.13. Wonderland Valley holds nearly half the climbing, followed by Central Wonderland and Near East. It is a quieter option than the roadside crags, though Wonderland Valley gets busy on weekends, and reaching the crags takes a long walk of 35 to 60 minutes.

ut_devil_s_playground_and_spires.blurb: Devil's Playground and the Spires lie in Utah's West Desert, north of the Bovine Mountains and northwest of the Great Salt Lake. The two main climbing zones sit about three miles apart, on granite crags. This is mostly a sport area, with a modest amount of trad and a small bouldering zone. Grades run from about 5.5 to 5.12, centered on 5.8 to 5.10, so it suits climbers at many levels. Devil's Fins, Aiguille du RV and Raven's Perch are the largest sectors, and Aiguille du RV is known for patina climbing. Spring is the prime season, with fall also good, while summers are hot unless you chase shade.

az_5_windy_ridge.blurb: Windy Ridge is a stretch of roadside crags high on the Catalina Highway in the Santa Catalina Mountains above Tucson, at about 6,500 feet. Sport climbing leads, followed by trad, with a good number of boulder problems. Grades center on 5.10 to 5.12, with a few easier lines and some at 5.13. Middle Earth is the standout sport crag, mixing steep, bouldery sections with vertical friction faces. Lonesome Pine, Goosehead and Cozzetti Crags add variety, and Secret Gully and Lizard Boulders hold the bouldering. Spring and fall are best, since summer can be too hot and winter cold. At Middle Earth the left side keeps shade until about three in the afternoon.

_expect.name: Capulin Canyon and Cochiti Mesa Area Crags

nm_capulin_canyon_and_cochiti_mesa_area_.blurb: These crags are on volcanic welded tuff in and around the Jemez Mountains of northern New Mexico. Capulin Canyon, the main draw, offers crack climbing in the style of Indian Creek, on cliffs up to about 200 feet, mostly trad with grades centered on 5.10 to 5.12. It is remote and far quieter than the better known desert crack areas. Cochiti Mesa has technical sport climbing on steep but not overhanging walls; it faces west and keeps shade until about noon. Eagle Canyon stays shaded nearly all day. Fall and spring are generally the best seasons, with the canyon at its best from October through May.

or_bend_area.blurb: Bend has the best ropeless climbing in Oregon, spread across many small boulder zones in the woods and along the Deschutes River rather than a few big ones. Nearly everything is bouldering, with problems from V0 up to V11, mostly V1 to V5 and a thinner layer of harder lines. Cascade Lakes Highway, the MBV Boulders, Skyliners Road and The Depot hold the most. Meadow Camp, on the highway, offers volcanic rock with pockets, crimps and cracks that can be rough on skin. Mile Marker 5 and The Depot stay shaded and cool in summer, which makes them good escapes from heat, while other spots sit in sun most of the day.
